help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:172  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:173  The first line answers the question the timer cannot: it reads the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:174  `run-state.json` written by the last `run-once` pass. Three distinct
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:175  answers, and only the first is a healthy one:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:176  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:177  * last run recent and successful -> exit 0
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:178  * last run FAILED -> exit 1, saying which step failed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:179  * no run recorded at all, or nothing has run for longer than
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:180    4x `backup_interval_secs` (minimum 1 hour) -> exit 1. A dead timer
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:181    usually leaves a *successful* last run behind, so this overdue check
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:182    is the only thing that catches it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:183  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:184  Never prints session content: counts, timestamps and digests only.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:189  machine holds three sessions or three thousand, so the verdict never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:190  scrolls away.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:196  Also print one metadata line per session found (can be hundreds).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:199  Print exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else (the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:202  `{"kind":"not_applicable",…}` — an unknown is never serialised as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:203  `0`, `null` or a missing field. `run_state.kind` is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:204  `known` / `missing` / `unreadable`; `scanner.kind` is `ok` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:205  `failed`. `exit_semantics` documents what the exit code means.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:305  Initialise a new destination as a *full extra copy* (ADR-013).

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:351  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:352  Metadata tier only: this walks snapshot/index/tree objects and never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:353  fetches or decrypts a data blob, which is why it is cheap. On a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:354  three-session fixture the metadata walk read 11,761 bytes against
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:355  1,206,285 bytes of data packs — two orders of magnitude apart. Use
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:356  `--cost` to see what a full-text pass over the current hits *would*
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:357  cost before asking for one; full-text matching is not implemented.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:358  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:359  One destination per run, always named: there is no automatic merge

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:364  destination and nothing matched, `3` could not finish reading it — so
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:365  "nothing matched" is unproven. `2` is a usage error, as elsewhere.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:403  Binds a short-lived HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` with an OS-assigned port
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:404  (never `0.0.0.0`, never a fixed port), prints the URL, optionally opens
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:405  your browser, and exits when idle or on Ctrl+C. Nothing is installed:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:406  no launchd, no systemd, no background process, no resident daemon.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:407  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:408  THREAT, stated plainly: loopback is NOT a security boundary. Every other
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:409  program running on this machine can connect to `127.0.0.1`, so this is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:410  not "safe because it's local". Access is gated by a random token that is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:411  generated fresh on every launch and appears only in the printed URL —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:412  never in a file, never in a log. Requests without that exact token are
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:413  refused (403), and any method other than GET is refused (405). Treat the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:414  URL as a secret for the lifetime of the process.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:415  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:416  Metadata tier only, same as `search`: machine, first 8 chars of the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:516  Seal one file already inside our stage into the next sealed-shard slot.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:542  Session id to seal into. Default: the active file's stem.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:545  Maximum sealed shards per bucket (default: 20).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:549  Reclaim the sealed shard body from the staging tree, but only where the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:550  archive provably holds every byte (ADR-020 Phase 4).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:551  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:552  The stage is an unbounded local full copy; nothing ever shrinks it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:553  This command retires the shard body once every declared destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:554  proves it holds each session. Proof means asking the archive itself —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:555  never the local cursor — for every session's digest triple (shard
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:556  count / concatenated bytes / concatenated sha256) and matching it
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:557  against the stage. A destination that cannot be consulted is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:558  "unproven" and blocks the reap: it is never treated as "does not have
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:559  it". Every declared destination must prove it holds each session, or
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:560  nothing is deleted.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:561  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:562  Default is a dry run that reports what would be reclaimed and deletes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:563  nothing; pass `--apply` to actually remove the body. `--apply` writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:564  each machine's retained summaries first, then deletes session by
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:565  session, keeping each session's persistent `shard-seq` counter so the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:566  next sequence never falls back onto archived shard names.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:567  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:568  Exit codes: 0 = reclaimable (dry run) or reclaimed (apply); 1 =
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:569  blocked — at least one destination is unreachable, partial, or fails
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:570  to hold a session, so nothing was deleted; 2 = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:572  Stage directory that holds the sealed `sessions/` tree.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:575  Actually delete the proven shard body. Default: dry run (report only).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:578  Repository path override (single-destination config only).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:581  Masterkey file override (single-destination config only).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:584  Concurrency cap override (single-destination config only).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:587  Backend option `key=value`, repeatable (single-destination config only).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:590  Disable ssh connection reaping after this run (for troubleshooting).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:594  Register this executable as the browsers' Native Messaging host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:595  (ADR-014 step 2) — or, with `--uninstall`, remove that registration.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:596  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:597  ADR-014 exists because `chrome.downloads` with `saveAs: false` is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:598  overridden by the browser-level "ask where to save each file before
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:599  downloading" preference, which no extension flag can suppress. At up to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:600  200 backfilled conversations a day that is 200 modal dialogs.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:601  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:602  This is one command instead of the five physical actions Native
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:603  Messaging otherwise costs: it renders the host manifest (`name` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:604  `description` / the absolute `path` of *this* executable / `type:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:605  stdio` / the pinned extension allowlist) and drops it into each
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:606  installed browser's discovery directory. No elevation: everything is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:607  per-user.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:608  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:609  Every path written, left alone, skipped or removed is printed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:610  absolutely. "No error" is not the same claim as "a file landed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:611  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:612  Idempotent: run it twice and there is exactly one manifest per browser,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:613  byte-identical, exit 0 both times. Exit codes: 0 = at least one manifest
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:614  is in place (or, for `--uninstall`, removal finished), 3 = nothing was
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:615  written because no known browser was found, 2 = usage error (bad host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:616  name / extension id / relative binary path), 1 = an action failed.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:618  Browser to register with, repeatable. Default: every browser whose
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:619  data directory exists on this machine. Naming one explicitly writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:620  it even when that directory is absent.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:623  Discovery root override (macOS default: `~/Library/Application
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:624  Support`). This is what makes the command testable without writing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:625  into a real browser directory.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:628  Which OS path layout to use. Default: this platform.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:631  Host binary recorded in the manifest. Default: this executable
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:632  (`std::env::current_exe()`), which is the only value that stays
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:633  correct after `cargo install --force`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:636  Host name override. Chromium's grammar is `[a-z0-9_.]` only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:639  Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave/Vivaldi extension id.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:642  Firefox add-on id (`browser_specific_settings.gecko.id`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:645  Remove the manifests this command writes — and nothing else.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:648  Windows only: skip the `reg.exe` step and only write the JSON.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:652  The Native Messaging host process itself.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:653  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:654  The framed stdio message loop is NOT implemented in this build. This
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:655  subcommand exists so that the registration above points at something
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:656  verifiable: `--self-test` prints one line of JSON on stdout and exits 0,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:657  which is how "does the host actually start?" is answered on a real
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:658  machine and in later tickets. Without `--self-test` it exits 2 rather
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:659  than pretending to serve a connection.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:660  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:661  Nothing but that one line may ever reach stdout: Chromium reads stdout
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:662  as a `u32` frame length, so a stray log line is read as a multi-gigabyte
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:663  frame and kills the pipe. Diagnostics go to stderr.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:665  Print one line of JSON describing this host, then exit 0.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:669  Build the activity sidecar index for one machine partition (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:670  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:671  Walks `<stage>/sessions/<machine>/<session>/<bucket>/NNNNNN.jsonl`,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:672  concatenates each session's shards in global sequence order, and feeds
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:673  every line through the conversation-time extractor to produce one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:674  `ActivityRow` per session. The rows are written as JSONL to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:675  `<stage>/meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl` — the file the `overview`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:676  command reads back out of a destination.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:677  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:678  The harness label is inferred from the session directory name: the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:679  canonical archived ids are `<source>.<machine>.<native-id>`, so the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:680  harness is the leading dot-segment (`claude-code.<m>.<uuid>` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:681  `claude-code`); short forms are handled too (`opencode~abc123` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:682  `opencode`, `cursor.d~xxx` -> `cursor`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:683  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:684  Metadata only: the extraction keeps a timestamp per line and throws the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:685  line away. Nothing else about a conversation is ever read, kept or
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:686  printed — the report is counts and the output path only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:687  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:688  Exit codes: `0` = the whole partition was read and the index written;
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:689  `3` = the stage could not be read (or reading was interrupted) — nothing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:690  (complete) was written; `1` = every session was read but the index file
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:691  itself could not be written; `2` = usage error. Same family as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:692  `collect`/`search`: `3` means "did not finish / never started", `1`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:693  means "finished and then failed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:695  Stage directory that holds the sealed `sessions/` tree.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:698  Machine partition for `sessions/<machine>/…`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:699  Default: config `machine`, else this machine's identity (generated
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:700  on first use); use `--machine` explicitly to choose the partition.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:704  Write this machine's display-name declaration (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:705  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:706  Writes `<stage>/meta/<machine>/machine.json` — a `MachineDeclaration`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:707  that carries the human display name, the OS and a first-seen time. The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:708  machine partition is resolved exactly like every other command: config
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:709  `machine` first, then the identity file (generated when missing). The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:710  next `push` archives the whole stage root, so this file rides along.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:711  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:712  The display name is taken from `--display-name` when given; otherwise
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:713  the system's LocalHostName (`scutil --get LocalHostName` on macOS,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:714  `hostname` elsewhere) is used. If neither is available the field is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:715  written **empty** and the command says so — a name is never invented.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:716  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:717  Exit codes: `0` = the declaration was written; `3` = the machine
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:718  partition could not be resolved or the identity is unusable; `1` = the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:719  file could not be written; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:721  Stage directory to write the declaration into (`<stage>/meta/…`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:724  Human display name for this machine. Default: system LocalHostName.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:728  Give a dead or sold machine a display name (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:729  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:730  Writes `<stage>/meta/<target>/label-by-<local-identity>.json` — a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:731  `LabelRecord` expressing *this* machine's opinion about what `<target>`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:732  should be called. It exists for machines that can no longer declare for
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:733  themselves (sold, dead, in a different building). Each file has exactly
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:734  one writer, so concurrent machines never fight over it; the overview
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:735  shows the label with the latest `written_at_unix`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:736  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:737  Exit codes: `0` = the label was written; `3` = the local identity could
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:738  not be resolved; `1` = the file could not be written; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:740  Stage directory to write the label into (`<stage>/meta/…`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:743  Machine id (partition) being labelled, e.g. a 32-hex identity.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:746  Display-name override for the target.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:750  Draw the machine × harness activity overview of one destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:751  (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:752  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:753  Opens the destination repository, takes each host's newest snapshot
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:754  (the same cross-machine merge as `read --all-machines`), and for every
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:755  snapshot recursively finds the activity index files at
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:756  `meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl`. The paths carry each machine's own
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:757  absolute stage prefix, so they are matched by the trailing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:758  `meta` / `<machine>` / `activity-v1.jsonl` marker — never by a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:759  path. The indexes are parsed into overview rows and rendered as a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:760  machine × harness matrix, a time-unknown tally and a width-adaptive
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:761  heatmap. Prints counts, machine names and time spans only — never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:762  conversation content.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:763  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:764  A machine that has a snapshot but **no** activity index is listed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:765  explicitly as "index missing" — it never vanishes silently, because a missing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:766  index is not the same thing as "that machine had no sessions".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:767  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:768  Exit codes: `0` = at least one index was read and rendered; `1` = the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:769  whole repository was read and there is no activity index at all (a real
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:770  "there is none", not a failure to look); `3` = the repository could not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:771  be read in full (open / snapshot / tree / dump failure) — the absences
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:772  below are unproven; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:774  Destination to open. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:775  there is no default destination.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:778  Terminal width for the matrix/heatmap (default: 100).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:781  Print exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else (the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:782  human matrix/heatmap is suppressed). Per-session `first_unix` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:783  `last_unix` and `time_source` are tri-state tagged
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:784  `{"kind":"known",…}` / `{"kind":"unknown","why":…}` — an unknown
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:785  time is never `null`. `no_index_anywhere` is `true` on exit 1
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:786  (read in full, no index anywhere); a failed read (exit 3) puts the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:787  reason in `error`.
